report_excerpt: **Level 7 — recursive cost lemma.** Both complete proof paragraphs were checked independently. A level-L call terminates by the finite exact solve. Downward induction through each finite positive integer nu_l establishes termination at all levels. One root and exactly nu_l children per level-l visit give v0=1 and v(l+1)=nu_l v(l), including L=1 and V/W choices. For fixed per-visit charges, disjoint allocation to executing visits proves the stated sum. Parent local work excludes child execution; repeated coarse residuals belong to the parent and all outer stopping checks are additional. The Statement explicitly requires actual-visit summation when counts/costs vary. Inherited relaxation counts use N_l and N_(l+1), including the boundary F assignment. No AC, contraction or speedup is inferred. `accepted_repair` links this actual new proof to original `refuter:77:1`; it is not creator self-acceptance or a metadata-only disposition.

proof_steps.claim: A call on level $L$ terminates by the stipulated finite exact forward solve. If calls on level $\ell+1$ terminate, [F1] makes a finite number $\nu_\ell$ of them and otherwise executes only finite local operations, so a level $\ell$ call terminates. Downward induction proves termination on level $0$. There is one root call and every level $\ell$ visit has exactly $\nu_\ell$ children, giving the stated visit recurrence.

Each noncoarsest visit has its stated local work charge, and every coarsest visit costs $W_L$. Partition all operations by their unique executing visit and sum the charges to obtain $W$. At level $\ell$ the inherited relaxation has $N_f=N_\ell$ and $N_c=N_{\ell+1}$, so [F2] supplies its three call counts, including the boundary assignment without a call. The data dependencies in [F1] and in each relaxation/forward solve require the stated scheduling order. Summing actual visit charges also covers unequal costs, and outer checks are outside the recursive call.
